access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: btclib-wallet is a library with no user interface. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/README.md
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses, citing the file, test or workflow behind each claim. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: integration-bitcoind.yml runs the regtest tests against Bitcoin Core on every pull request and push to main, with no path filter. test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and push to main that changes more than prose: its changes job skips the suite on a pull request that edits only the files its prose-pattern lists, and a push to main that changes only root Markdown files does not start it. Both are required checks on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag. It passes only if the rebuilt file matches the release's attested digest byte for byte. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit. Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its signed tag and verifies it against the release's build attestation, and RELEASING.md gives the same check to anyone. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_standard_variables_justification: This tree is pure Python on the uv_build backend and builds no native binary, so no compiler or linker runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from the Co-Authored-By trailer on AI-assisted commits, most of them fametrano's. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, did the 2026-09-30 security review and has contributed some changes. mayankdhingra02 opened 17 merged pull requests in October 2026, about 500 lines under src/ and 4,000 under tests/, on BIP322, PSBT and descriptors. Other outside contributors have made only small changes. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit to this repository. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: The organization's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md applies here, and GitHub's community profile of this repository shows it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy are pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs .pre-commit-config.yaml as a required check on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff] selects every rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and [tool.mypy] is strict. CONTRIBUTING.md names both and the commands that enforce them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: The significant contributors are fametrano, pmazzocchi and mayankdhingra02. pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. mayankdhingra02 opened 17 merged pull requests in October 2026, about 500 lines under src/ and 4,000 under tests/, on BIP322, PSBT and descriptors. Whether he is unassociated is not established. Other outside contributors have made only small changes. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit to this repository. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi https://github.com/mayankdhingra02
copyright_per_file_justification: Every .py file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: A wallet signs what the consensus rules define, and Bitcoin's consensus rules fix secp256k1, SHA-256 and the signature schemes. Another algorithm needs a soft fork first, and the project follows one when it activates. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography is delegated to ecc and btclib, not reimplemented.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: TlsLineTransport uses ssl.create_default_context(), which verifies the certificate chain and host name. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/fetch/transport.py
crypto_credential_agility_justification: btclib_wallet.fetch.bitcoin_core re-exports bitcoin-core-rpc's cookie_auth, COOKIE_USER and DEFAULT_DATADIR, so a BitcoinCoreFetcher can authenticate with Bitcoin Core's cookie file, read at each call, and the credential changes without a code change. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/fetch/bitcoin_core.py
crypto_keylength_justification: Keys are secp256k1 keys, about 128 bits of security, and BIP39 entropy is at least 128 bits, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030. TLS uses Python's default context, whose security level 2 refuses keys under 112 bits. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl
crypto_pfs_justification: TLS uses Python's default context, which since Python 3.10 disables cipher suites without forward secrecy; the floor here is 3.11. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl
crypto_published_justification: Cryptography is delegated to ecc and btclib, which implement published algorithms. ecc calls Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1 through btclib-secp256k1 when installed.
crypto_random_justification: BIP38 salts and seeds come from Python's secrets module, and mnemonic entropy from bip39-slip39, which uses secrets or os.urandom. Signing is ecc's: RFC 6979 nonces, and BIP340 auxiliary randomness from secrets. random.Random is used only in coin selection, to shuffle and draw the candidate UTXOs, and makes no key or nonce. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/tree/main/src/btclib_wallet
crypto_tls12_justification: TlsLineTransport sets minimum_version to TLS 1.2 itself. The Esplora and Core backends use bitcoin-core-rpc's HTTPS. CompactFilterFetcher's p2p transport does not use TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/fetch/transport.py
crypto_used_network_justification: Not every network communication has a secure protocol. CompactFilterFetcher talks to a peer over plain TCP, the p2p v1 transport, and no encrypted transport is offered for it; its transport has no default, so the caller chooses it, and its messages are checked against what the fetcher holds. Elsewhere traffic goes in the clear only where the caller chooses it. TlsLineTransport, the Electrum transport, verifies the server certificate and host name with a TLS 1.2 floor, and offers no plain TCP. The Esplora backend has no default server. The BLOCKSTREAM_INFO constant it offers holds https urls. The Core backends use the caller's bitcoin-core-rpc client, which verifies HTTPS and speaks plain HTTP only for an http url. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/fetch/peer_transport.py https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/fetch/transport.py https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/fetch/esplora.py
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: TlsLineTransport completes the TLS handshake before it writes the request line. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/fetch/transport.py
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Signing runs through ecc, on SHA-256 (RFC 6979, BIP340). BIP38's AES-256 is supplied by the caller, and SECURITY.md says that BIP38 has no MAC by its own specification. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution channels (GitHub, PyPI) use HTTPS exclusively.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases and their hashes are served over HTTPS only, from PyPI and GitHub.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot's version updates are configured in .github/dependabot.yml, and its security updates are on. CodeQL and OpenSSF Scorecard also run on a schedule. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: btclib-wallet goes from a seed to a signed, broadcast bitcoin transaction, on top of the btclib library. https://btclib.org/btclib-wallet/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md shows and links the OpenSSF Best Practices and Baseline badges under its opening paragraph, and the Scorecard badge in its Status section. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents which module holds what, the btclib-org packages it depends on (btclib, ecc, base58-bech32, bip39-slip39, bitcoin-core-rpc) and why each, and every place a module reaches outside the process: HWI's subprocess and the fetch backends' sockets. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_current_justification: The API reference is generated from the docstrings, and docs.yml builds it with -W -n as a required check on every pull request. tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md's *Installing* and *An address from a mnemonic* sections walk a new user through a first use. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/README.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's *Where constant time ends* says which operations reach libsecp256k1, that secrets are not zeroized, that BIP38 has no MAC and where randomness comes from. *A backend is trusted, and not every backend alike* says how far each fetch backend's answers are checked. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The tests, mutation runs and fuzz targets run Python without -O, so assertions are enabled.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open, and the weekly fuzz and mutation runs on main pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published. release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing also run every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree is pure Python, a memory-safe language. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
external_dependencies_justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, in btclib-org/.github, documents how decisions are made and every role; README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site is served over HTTPS and answers Content-Security-Policy with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security. Check with curl -sI https://btclib.org/btclib-wallet/ The repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page https://pypi.org/project/btclib-wallet/ sends all but the CSP; that is PyPI's to set. The documentation site https://btclib-wallet.readthedocs.io/ is served by Read the Docs over HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options; that is Read the Docs' to set. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-01.
hardening_justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so unsafe deserialization, weak temporary files and shell injection fail the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md argues each secure-design principle against this tree, and ARCHITECTURE.md lays out the signing boundary and the backends a wallet trusts; SECURITY.md applies it where constant time ends and to what a backend is trusted with. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
input_validation_justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid; the unchecked work lives in a private twin the public function calls once it has validated, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_common_justification: pip install btclib-wallet installs it from PyPI, and pip uninstall removes it; README.md gives the command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/README.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: uv sync installs the development environment in one command; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives it beside the gates. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is pip install, which follows pip's own conventions for where files go; the project has no installer of its own. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: Output is technical data (hex, addresses, PSBTs), and the package has no interactive prompt or user interface meant for localization. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/README.md
know_common_errors_justification: fametrano, the primary developer, maintains ASSURANCE_CASE.md, whose Common implementation weaknesses section names each CWE that matters here and what counters it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#common-implementation-weaknesses
know_secure_design_justification: fametrano, the primary developer, maintains ASSURANCE_CASE.md, whose Secure design principles section applies each principle to this code. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles
license_per_file_justification: Every .py file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/src/btclib_wallet/__init__.py
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported, and nothing is backported, as SECURITY.md's *Supported versions* says. RELEASE_NOTES.md says, for each breaking change, what a user has to change. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and allows only secure second factors (TOTP, security keys/passkeys, GitHub Mobile; no SMS), so no account can read or change a repository's sensitive settings without MFA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset has a deletion rule with no bypass actor, and branch protection sets allow_deletions to false, so nobody can delete main. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at both the organization and the repository, and GitHub Actions cannot approve pull requests; every workflow also declares permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Untrusted event fields and dispatch inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. On issue_comment, the mention job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: A workflow_dispatch input is either mutation.yml's profile, a choice from a fixed list, or verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique calendar version, YYYY.M.D, set by a signed v* tag. release.yml's version-check job refuses a tag that differs from the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name, and the attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/releases/latest
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib-wallet.readthedocs.io/.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS-only; PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle, so a tampered download fails verification. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-wallet/
osps_br_04_01_justification: Every release carries CHANGELOG.md's entry (every change) and RELEASE_NOTES.md's (what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included); the GitHub release body is the release notes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation, and each GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push with a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run against .secrets.baseline in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_do_01_01_justification: README.md's Installing and An address from a mnemonic sections give the first use. The API reference is at https://btclib-wallet.readthedocs.io/. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/README.md
osps_do_02_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report issue form (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) asks for what a report needs; SECURITY.md routes a vulnerability away from the public tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
osps_do_03_01_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release files. RELEASING.md adds the offline --bundle form and a rebuild from the tag that passes only if its digests match the attested ones. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_03_02_justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command, with --owner btclib-org, --signer-workflow naming the organization's reusable-build.yml and --source-ref the release tag, and a compare of the certificate's sourceRepositoryIdentifier with this repository's id, which a rename keeps. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions* states that a release stops receiving security updates as soon as the next one is published, since only the latest is supported and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: pyproject.toml says beside each runtime dependency why it is one, and ARCHITECTURE.md's *The dependencies* says why each sibling package is one. Dependencies come from PyPI through uv, are pinned in uv.lock, and Dependabot updates them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_do_07_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives uv sync, which creates the environment from uv.lock, and says uv is the only tool that must be installed. *Reproducing what CI runs* gives uv build, which produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_01_02_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: where an issue is filed, one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_le_01_01_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-wallet/
osps_le_03_01_justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/commits/main
osps_qa_02_01_justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every release attaches a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM, <name>-<version>.cdx.json, built from the wheel and covered by the release attestation. It lists both files' SHA-256, the license and the declared dependencies. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/releases/latest
osps_qa_03_01_justification: main requires the CI status checks. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far
osps_qa_04_02_justification: Each release is built from this single repository; the sibling packages it depends on are released separately from their own repositories, which are held to the same standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No executable is committed. The binary files are test vectors and fuzz seeds in Bitcoin's own serialization, and the docs' copy of Python's Sphinx inventory; check-added-large-files runs in the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The binary files are test vectors and fuzz seeds in Bitcoin's own serialization, and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, Python's Sphinx inventory. tests/_data/README.md pins the blocks to their source, and docs/source/conf.py gives the command that fetches the inventory. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/tests/_data/README.md
osps_qa_06_01_justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') is a required status check on main; test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request that changes more than prose, as automated_integration_testing says. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite, and *What gates a merge, and what only reports* gives which workflows run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage, stated in CONTRIBUTING.md, and pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author before a merge to main, and dismisses an approval on a new push. Its bypass list holds one actor, fametrano, in pull_request mode, at rest: the organization-wide bypass the maintainer kept on 2026-11-04 (btclib-org/.github#2021 and btclib-org/.github#2040), read with gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/rulesets on 2026-11-11. btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md reserves that bypass for an emergency, and it is used for ordinary work: over the last two releases, 41 of the 44 pull requests merged had no approval from anybody other than their author (v2026.11.11 23 of 24, v2026.11.7 18 of 20). https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_sa_01_01_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the components, their layering and every place the software reaches outside the process, and ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Trust boundaries* and *Threat model* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The API reference at https://btclib-wallet.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module (ruff's D rules require them, and a docs test fails when a shipped module is missing from the reference); CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* states what is public.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered. SECURITY.md's *Where constant time ends* and *A backend is trusted, and not every backend alike* record the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md#where-constant-time-ends
osps_sa_03_02_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. A report triaged as easy to rediscover is fixed as soon as possible, and its advisory is published with the fix. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/security/advisories/new
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a runtime dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_05_02_justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing
osps_vm_05_03_justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a runtime dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_vm_06_01_justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request: ruff with the bandit S rules, strict mypy, zizmor and detect-secrets. Any finding blocks the merge unless suppressed at its site with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request, but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: A merged pull request that changes code under src/ also changes tests/, unless it leaves behaviour as it was: a docstring, a comment, a move, a removal or a refactor. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
release_notes_vulns_justification: The release notes name the GHSA id of each advisory published by the time of the release: v2026.10.18 to v2026.11.11 fix none and name none; v2026.10.4 names GHSA-qq38-77mp-j6wr and GHSA-v4gq-j2v2-c4jp, v2026.10.7 names GHSA-v4gq-j2v2-c4jp, whose fix it completes, v2026.10.8 names GHSA-62jf-v327-86h5, and v2026.10.9 names GHSA-8qrf-j8jh-cx23. v2026.10.16 describes the fix of GHSA-4x2v-6p43-cq6x and links its issue, but not the id: the advisory was published 86 minutes after the release. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/releases/tag/v2026.11.11
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
repo_interim_justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
report_process_justification: Bugs are reported in GitHub Issues, through the bug-report form. CONTRIBUTING.md's The issue tracker says where, and SECURITY.md takes vulnerabilities instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/issues https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-issue-tracker
report_tracker_justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/issues
require_2FA_justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member (organization setting two_factor_requirement_enabled = true), so nobody without 2FA can change a repository. https://github.com/btclib-org
roles_responsibilities_justification: btclib-org/.github's GOVERNANCE.md, *Roles*, names the maintainer, the owners, repository administrators and collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
secure_2FA_justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and has 'Only allow secure two-factor methods' selected, which refuses SMS as a second factor: only TOTP apps, security keys/passkeys and GitHub Mobile are accepted. Read from the organization's security settings on 2026-09-30 and recorded at https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
security_review_justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the tree on 2026-09-30 against ASSURANCE_CASE.md, claim by claim. Issue 169 records the scope, the method, what was not covered and the findings, each filed as an issue. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/issues/169
signed_releases_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation, and each GitHub release a Sigstore provenance bundle. Every release tag is signed. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/releases/latest
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites are btclib.org, a static GitHub Pages site, GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; none of these repositories runs a site of its own that stores user passwords -- authentication is GitHub's and PyPI's, not this project's. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
small_tasks_justification: Small tasks for newcomers carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-issue-tracker https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: ruff, a FLOSS tool, runs select = ["ALL"], bandit's S rules included, in the required lint check. CodeQL also runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has one open alert, actions/untrusted-checkout on qa-assets.yml, open since 2026-11-05 and not yet triaged (btclib-org/btclib-wallet#784). ruff and mypy findings block the merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: lint.yml (ruff, mypy) and codeql.yml run on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/actions/workflows/lint.yml
test_branch_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets branch = true in [tool.coverage.run], and the 100% gate includes branch coverage. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and push to main that changes more than prose, as automated_integration_testing says, and its aggregate check is required on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
test_justification: 100% coverage floor, enforced locally and in CI: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/actions/workflows/test.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% coverage, and pyproject.toml's fail_under = 100.0 fails the required test check when new code has no test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 in [tool.coverage.report], and the required test check enforces it on every pull request that changes more than prose, as automated_integration_testing says. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
test_statement_coverage90_justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 in [tool.coverage.report], and the coverage job gates every pull request that changes more than prose, as automated_integration_testing says. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
tests_are_added_justification: The required check test: every job passed fails any pull request that leaves a line or branch untested. The merged pull requests show recent changes landing with their tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% coverage of every change, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: Over the last two releases, v2026.11.7 and v2026.11.11, 3 of 44 pull requests were approved by somebody other than the author, 7%, below the 50% the criterion asks (v2026.11.11 1 of 24, v2026.11.7 2 of 20); 0 were approved by somebody other than fametrano. Counted by merge time between release publications, over the same two-release window on every btclib-org project. main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano holds a pull_request-mode bypass of it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock. Dependabot updates them weekly, and deps-latest runs the suite weekly against their latest releases. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml
version_semver_justification: Calendar versioning, YYYY.M.D, with the day as the micro level; each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing
version_tags_signed_justification: Every release tag is signed, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/tags
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No publicly known vulnerability is left unfixed: each published advisory names the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/security/advisories
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Every published advisory names the release that fixes it, and no Dependabot alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: An advisory credits its reporter as finder: pmazzocchi on GHSA-qq38-77mp-j6wr and GHSA-v4gq-j2v2-c4jp, and on GHSA-62jf-v327-86h5, where the credit awaits his acceptance. fametrano, the maintainer, filed the other two. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/security/advisories
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: GHSA-qq38-77mp-j6wr and GHSA-v4gq-j2v2-c4jp, reported privately by pmazzocchi on 2026-09-30, were answered with v2026.10.4 on 2026-10-04. v2026.10.7 completed the GHSA-v4gq-j2v2-c4jp fix on 2026-10-07. GHSA-4x2v-6p43-cq6x, found by fametrano (issue 415, 2026-10-15), was fixed in v2026.10.16 and published on 2026-10-16. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/security/advisories
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or security at btclib dot org, says who can see a report and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_strict_justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are required, zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again in the lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-wallet/blob/main/pyproject.toml
